# Error catalogue

<p class="pm-kind"><b>Reference · generated</b> · every public error type in the workspace, variant by variant, with the meaning its documentation states</p>

The table is read from the source, so a variant that exists is listed and a variant that is gone disappears. The troubleshooting guide gives remedies for the errors a user meets from the command line.

## `ShmError` in `core/core-region`

Defined in `core/core-region/src/lib.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Open` | `shm_open(3)`, `fstat(2)` or a header read failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `Truncate` | `ftruncate` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `NoSpace` | Linux could not reserve a new region's page: `posix_fallocate(3)` failed, with `ENOSPC` on a full `/dev/shm`, `ENOMEM`, or `EINTR` after [`RESERVE_ATTEMPTS`] tries. The object was unlinked and nothing was mapped. Never returned off Linux. |
| `Map` | `mmap` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `InvalidName` | The name contains a NUL byte. |
| `RegionTooSmall` | The object is smaller than a region, [`REGION_SIZE`] bytes. |
| `LayoutMismatch` | The header is not a region's: the magic is not `PMRG` (not a region, or not yet published), or the layout version is not [`LAYOUT_VERSION`]. Nothing was mapped. |

## `NumaError` in `core/core-region`

Defined in `core/core-region/src/numa.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HugePageAlloc` | Making a memfd ([`allocate_hugepage_memfd`]) or duplicating a descriptor ([`dup_fd`]) failed; the string says what and why. |
| `NumaPin` | Pinning a thread or binding memory to a NUMA node failed: `sched_setaffinity(2)` or `mbind(2)` refused, the node is past the 64 a binding can name, or a CPU number is past the `CPU_SETSIZE` (1024) a `cpu_set_t` can name. |
| `UnsupportedPageSize` | Caller requested a page size the kernel doesn't expose. Check `/sys/kernel/mm/hugepages` to see what's available. |
| `LibnumaMissing` | The operation is Linux-only: binding memory, detecting a node, pinning a thread and hugepage memfds return this elsewhere. Nothing links libnuma; on Linux these are the kernel's system calls. |
| `Io` | Underlying I/O failure (typically while creating or sizing the SHM file). |

## `Error` in `core/core-region`

Defined in `core/core-region/src/shm.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Open` | `shm_open(3)` or the `fstat(2)` after it failed; the field is its `errno` (`EEXIST` from an exclusive creation whose name already holds an object, `ENOENT` from an open of a name that holds none, `EACCES` from a runtime that refuses POSIX shared memory, `EBADF` from a descriptor that is not open). |
| `Truncate` | `ftruncate(2)` could not size the new object; the field is its `errno` (`EFBIG`, `ENOSPC`). |
| `NoSpace` | Linux could not reserve a new object's pages: `posix_fallocate(3)` failed, with `ENOSPC` on a full `/dev/shm`, `ENOMEM`, or `EINTR` after [`RESERVE_ATTEMPTS`] tries. Never returned off Linux. |
| `Map` | `mmap(2)` failed; the field is its `errno`. |
| `InvalidName` | The name holds a NUL byte, which no C string can carry. |
| `TooSmall` | The object is shorter than the caller needs: `have` bytes where `need` are needed. An object at size zero is one a creator has made and not yet sized. |

## `RingError` in `core/core-ring`

Defined in `core/core-ring/src/lib.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Open` | `shm_open(3)`, `fstat(2)` or a header read failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `Truncate` | `ftruncate` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `NoSpace` | Linux could not reserve a new ring's pages: `posix_fallocate(3)` failed, with `ENOSPC` on a full `/dev/shm`, `ENOMEM`, or `EINTR` after [`RESERVE_ATTEMPTS`] tries. Nothing was mapped: a creator by name unlinked its object, and [`PulseRing::from_fd`] left the descriptor open and unformatted. Never returned off Linux. |
| `Map` | `mmap` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `Unlink` | `shm_unlink` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `InvalidName` | The ring name contains a NUL byte, or is not a valid hub name. |
| `InvalidCapacity` | Zero slots; or, from a constructor that sizes or formats a region, a ring whose size, `HEADER_SIZE + capacity × slot size`, does not fit a `usize` and a file offset. Nothing was created, opened or mapped. |
| `BatchTooLarge` | A batch publish was given more pulses than the ring has slots; nothing was written. Publish at most `capacity` pulses per batch. |
| `Stalled` | A blocking publish waited its whole timeout and the slowest reader never freed the room it needed: it stopped, died, or there is none. Nothing was published, so the call can be retried. |
| `NoReaderTable` | [`PulseRing::register_reader`] on a ring made without a reader table. |
| `ReadersFull` | Every line of the ring's reader table is taken. |
| `InvalidReaders` | A reader table of `max_readers` lines: it needs from 1 to [`MAX_READERS`]. Nothing was created. |
| `NameTooLong` | A derived shared-memory name exceeds the platform limit. |
| `RegionTooSmall` | The object is smaller than the ring the caller asked to map, which would fault past its end. |
| `LayoutMismatch` | The header does not describe the ring the caller maps: the magic is not `PMSR` (not a ring, or not yet formatted), or the layout version, capacity or slot size differs. |
| `CrcMismatch` | [`PulseRing::read_slot_verify_crc`] found a slot whose CRC32C trailer does not match its data. |

## `EnvelopeStoreError` in `core/core-store`

Defined in `core/core-store/src/lib.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Open` | `shm_open(3)`, `fstat(2)` or a header read failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `Truncate` | `ftruncate` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `NoSpace` | Linux could not reserve a new store's pages: `posix_fallocate(3)` failed, with `ENOSPC` on a full `/dev/shm`, `ENOMEM`, or `EINTR` after [`RESERVE_ATTEMPTS`] tries. The object was unlinked and nothing was mapped. Never returned off Linux. |
| `Map` | `mmap` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `Unlink` | `shm_unlink` failed; the field is the `errno`. |
| `InvalidName` | The name contains a NUL byte. |
| `InvalidCapacity` | Zero slots, more than the header's 32-bit capacity field can record, or so many that `64 + capacity × slot size` does not fit a `usize` and a file offset. Nothing was opened, created or mapped. |
| `RegionTooSmall` | The object is smaller than the store the caller asked to map, or, for [`EnvelopeStore::open_existing`], than a header or the store its header describes. |
| `LayoutMismatch` | The header does not describe the layout this build uses. |
| `SlotBusy` | Each of the [`CLAIM_ATTEMPTS`] cursors tried found its slot held or taken by a newer lap, or named a lap too large to mark (a write cursor corrupted in shared memory). Nothing was written; readers skip every cursor given up. |
| `InvalidIndex` | An index of `buckets` buckets for a store of `capacity` slots: the count must be a power of two no larger than the capacity rounded up to one. Nothing was created. |
| `EnvelopeTooLarge` | The envelope's canonical encoding exceeds [`MAX_ENTRY_SIZE`] bytes. |

## `TransportError` in `core/core-transport`

Defined in `core/core-transport/src/lib.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Io` | Underlying I/O failure (socket, file, kernel). |
| `BufferTooSmall` | The caller's envelope buffer is smaller than the incoming envelope. |
| `Decode` | A frame failed the wire format's validation (magic, version, length, CRC, or the backend's own checks). |
| `EnvelopeTooLarge` | The envelope exceeds the transport's `max_envelope()`. |
| `Send` | A send failed for a reason `Io` does not fit, such as the backend's flow control stalling (the UDP transport's backpressure window, which its opt-in congestion control sizes). |
| `Recv` | A receive failed for a reason `Io` and `Decode` do not fit. |

| Variant | Meaning |

## `SenderError` in `core/pulse-wire-udp`

Defined in `core/pulse-wire-udp/src/sender.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Io` | Underlying socket I/O failure. |
| `Encode` | The frame failed to encode: [`WireError::EnvelopeTooLarge`] for an envelope over [`Sender::envelope_limit`]. The sender does not fragment. |
| `NoDestination` | No destination — caller must `connect()` or use [`Sender::send_to`]. |
| `Stalled` | Backpressure held the send past `stall_timeout`: the receiver's cursor did not come within `target_queue_depth` frames of the next sequence number. The frame was not sent and its sequence number not used, so the call can be retried. |
| `InvalidQueueDepth` | [`Sender::enable_backpressure`] was given a `target_queue_depth` of zero, which admits no frame; the sender's backpressure stays as it was. |
| `Seal` | Sealing is installed and the frame could not be sealed: [`SealError::NoSession`] when no session to the destination is in use ([`Sealing::connect`] first). Found before the send waits on backpressure; the frame was not sent and its sequence number not used. |

## `BatchSendError` in `core/pulse-wire-udp`

Defined in `core/pulse-wire-udp/src/sender.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FrameError` | The frame at `index` failed: its encode, a backpressure stall past `stall_timeout`, or its send (on Linux, a `sendmmsg(2)` failure after earlier frames went out). The frames before `index` were sent; the rest were not. |
| `BatchTooLarge` | The batch is longer than [`MAX_BATCH_FRAMES`]. Nothing was sent. |
| `PartialSend` | `sendmmsg(2)` took fewer frames than it was given (Linux): the first `sent` were sent, the rest not. The kernel drops the error of any frame after a call's first, so resending the tail is how to learn it. |
| `Io` | `sendmmsg(2)` returned -1 for the batch's first frame (Linux); carries the underlying `errno`. Nothing was sent. |

## `WireError` in `core/pulse-wire-udp`

Defined in `core/pulse-wire-udp/src/wire.rs`.

| Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BufferTooSmall` | The buffer is shorter than a frame with no envelope, [`HEADER_BYTES`] + [`TRAILER_BYTES`]. |
| `InvalidEnvelopeLength` | The frame declares an envelope longer than [`MAX_ENVELOPE`] or than the buffer holds. |
| `BadMagic` | Magic mismatch — datagram is not a pulse-wire-udp frame. |
| `UnsupportedVersion` | Version mismatch. |
| `CrcMismatch` | CRC32C mismatch — wire-level bit-flip or mid-stream truncation; receivers count this toward loss metrics. |
| `EnvelopeTooLarge` | The envelope is too large for one datagram, or, from a sender with FEC on, for its window's parity to fit one; with fragmentation on, too large for a run of fragments. Refused before anything is sent, so the caller can chunk. |
| `InvalidFragment` | A fragment that disagrees with itself: an index or count out of range, a total length over [`crate::fragment::MAX_MESSAGE`], or a sequence number that is not its run's first plus its index ([`crate::fragment::decode_fragment`]). |
| `EnvelopeCodec` | A decoded [`Frame`]'s envelope bytes are not a canonical [`PulseEnvelope`]. Returned only by [`decode_with_envelope`]. |
| `EnvelopeIdMismatch` | The envelope decoded, but its content id is not the id of its type, name and payload: the frame passed its CRC, so the id is stale or forged. Returned only by [`decode_with_envelope`]. |
